messages.author: ecfda580123e3920
messages.subject: Bug of the QTL package?
parts:
Hi all,

I used the QTL package to scan QTLs in an F2 population. I want to use the CIM function with permutation to determine the cutoff of LOD value.
However, R sometimes crashed. The F2 population is small with only about 50 individuals. But I got thousand of traits (gene expression values).

The following is the error info:

 *** caught segfault ***
address 0x40c1, cause 'memory not mapped'

Traceback:
 1: .C("R_markerforwself2", as.integer(nrow(x)), as.integer(ncol(x)),     as.integer(x), as.double(y), as.integer(maxsize), chosen = as.integer(rep(0,         maxsize)), rss = as.double(rep(0, maxsize)), PACKAGE = "qtl")
 2: markerforwself2(g, y, n.marcovar)
 3: cim(cross, pheno.col = pheno.col, n.marcovar = n.marcovar, window = window,     method = method, imp.method = imp.method, error.prob = error.prob,     map.function = map.function)
 4: cim(data, method = "hk", pheno.col = i, n.perm = 500)


I don't know why. I am using Linux server with 64 GB memory.

Here is the code I used:

#### for test only
library(qtl)
data <- read.cross("csvsr", genfile = "Bin169.zs.geno.csv",
                   phefile = "Bin169.ase.csv", genotype =
                     c("1","2","0"), estimate.map = F )
calc.data = calc.genoprob(data, error.prob = 0.0001)
data = sim.geno(calc.data, error.prob = 0.0001)

for (i in 2:ncol(data$pheno)) {
  cat(i, "\n")
  cim( data, method = "hk", pheno.col = i, n.perm = 500)
}
#### 

The pheno file and the geno file are in the attachment.

I've been able to fix the cim() bug. 

The revised package is at https://github.com/kbroman/qtl and http://rqtl.org
I've submitted the revision to CRAN, but it will take a few days for it to appear.

karl
